note: Adapted from the revision of Sands (1965), originally in English; the original gives an alate description, while the soldier and worker descriptions are in other sections of the same work, and in the IA full text (a single text stream, unpaginated) the later part of this species is interleaved with the synonymy list, so only the alate part is included here; the measurement table is misaligned in the OCR text, so only the legible head-width range is recorded.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule, middle of the frons and vertex brown to dark sepia brown; vertex with 2 or 3 branching pale longitudinal stripes, the middle one often indistinct or absent; postclypeus, labrum, the region between the eyes and the base of the mandibles, and the narrowing longitudinal stripe above each eye orange yellow to brown, the pale area in front of the eye sometimes extending in front of the ocellus and along the posterior margin of the postclypeus; antennae orange yellow to brown. Pronotum orange yellow to yellowish brown, the anterior corners sometimes brown; mesonotum and metanotum yellow to orange yellow; the other thoracic sclerites and the legs yellow. Abdominal tergites brown to dark chestnut brown, darker around the spiracles and paler at the anterior corners, sternites pale yellow, sometimes brown around the spiracles. Wings translucent pale brown, the subcosta and radial sector yellow and in part with a brown outline at the base, the membrane behind the radial sector with yellow longitudinal streaks; the remaining veins fine brown or with a brown outline. Posterior margin of the head capsule much less than a semicircle behind the eyes, slightly undulate immediately behind the eyes; fontanelle small, paler than the head, short Y-shaped or shaped like an inverted A, sometimes with a small depression in front of or behind it, or its posterior part covered by darker cuticle, the lateral arms usually swollen at the apex; eyes oval, weakly to moderately projecting relative to their own diameter and medium-sized relative to the width of the head; ocelli medium-sized, oval, touching the eye or up to one third of their own shortest diameter away from it; postclypeus moderately inflated, 2.3—2.6 times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin convex and rounded, sometimes slightly indistinct in the middle; molar plate of the right mandible with 6—8 ridges; antennae 15—16 segments, occasionally 17, one fifth of the specimens with 15 but then the basal segments often partly subdivided, in the 16-segmented ones segments 2, 3, 5 and 6 about equal in length and longer than segment 4. The pale odoriferous patch on the anterior margin of abdominal sternite 5 is small, 0.35—0.64 mm wide and 0.13 mm long; cerci slightly shorter to slightly longer than their basal width, conical. Pilosity of the vertex unequal in length, the setae not forming felt or a pad. Measurements (12 localities, 36 individuals): head width 1.43—1.76 mm (mean 1.56).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands treated Eutermes terricola Trägårdh, 1904, Eutermes suspensus Silvestri, 1914 and Trinervitermes nigeriensis Sjöstedt, 1926 all as new synonyms of this species; the distinguishing characters of the species are the posterior margin of the head, the shape of the fontanelle, the proportions of the eyes and ocelli and the proportions of the postclypeus given above.
